text:
Alex: Heads-up — observed a regression in Mixtral v1.2 serving for long context (2k). Throughput drops ~40% compared to yesterday's baseline when serving models with nonstandard head_dim (70). Appears to be a kernel slowpath: fallback to SDPA/Triton. cc @Maria @Suresh :thinking_face:

Maria: Can you paste the kernel selection log and a small repro?

Alex: Sure, pasted logs below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T10:12:34Z] model=mixtral-70 head_dim=70 seq_len=2048 batch=4
[2026-03-18T10:12:34Z] kernel_selector: attempted flash_attn_v2 -> rejection: head_dim % 8 != 0
[2026-03-18T10:12:34Z] kernel_selector: attempting sdpa_triton
[2026-03-18T10:12:34Z] kernel_selector: chosen sdpa_triton (fallback reasons: unaligned_head_dim, mask_pad_alignment)
[2026-03-18T10:12:34Z] perf: tokens/s=18.2 p50=78ms p95=240ms
```

Alex: Baseline (head_dim=64): tokens/s=30.7 p50=46ms p95=120ms. Also seeing more frequent KV cache flushes (every 64 tokens) in the slow run — not sure if related.

Devon: Do you have the exact command to reproduce? small script?

Alex: Repro command we used:
```bash
./serve_infer --model mixtral-70 --seq_len 2048 --batch 4 --kv_cache=true --kv_prefetch=false --enable_kernel_hints=1
```
Reproducer script: gist link (internal) -> short loop that sends long prompts and measures throughput.

Suresh: This smells like the mask/padding alignment issue we saw with Qwen last quarter. SDPA route requires 16/32 block alignment on our Triton kernels so odd head widths fall back. Two concerns: (1) padding heads to multiple-of-8 might be fast but could break RoPE math if implemented naively, (2) fallback kernel path is doing extra memcpy+reshape which kills perf.

Maria: If we pad head_dim at runtime, we must apply a RoPE-aware transform (rotate/scale) so attention indices align. Has anyone tried headpad + RoPE rescale?

Alex: Quick experiment: set allow_unaligned_heads=true in runtime -> it forced flash_attn path and removed the Triton fallback. Throughput recovered to ~28 tok/s but memory went up ~12% and occasional NaN in gradients (serving-only run, so odd). Not safe for canary yet.

perf-bot: Auto-profile attached: kernel breakdown (single request): flash_attn path: kernel_time=35% memcpy=12% other=53% ; sdpa_triton path: kernel_time=72% memcpy=18% other=10% — end-to-end slower by 2.1x. (flamegraph link internal)

Devon: Short-term mitigation options: 1) runtime headpad to nearest multiple-of-8 and rewrite RoPE transform to apply only to effective dims, 2) improve Triton kernel to accept unaligned heads (expensive), 3) force small batching so flash_attn stays selected. Which is fastest to iterate?

Suresh: I'll prototype runtime headpad + RoPE-aware adjust in a branch. We should add a regression test that runs a small prompt through padded vs unpadded codepaths and diffs token outputs for drift beyond epsilon. If drift > 1e-6, reject.

Maria: Plan for infra work: (A) Add unit test for head_dim % 8 != 0 in kernel-selection; (B) Instrument KV cache codepath to log when we force a flush due to kernel change; (C) Canary runtime flag allow_headpad=true to dedicated pool only. I'll create the rollout checklist.

Alex: Assigning action items: Suresh -> prototype headpad+RoPE test; Maria -> tests + canary rollout plan; Devon -> repro script + perf baseline. I'll open the issue and a PR with logs + perf table. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Devon: One more note — if we can't get headpad production-ready quickly, consider a temporary optimizer in model importer: if head_dim nonstandard, offer quantized variant with 64 head_dim mapping until proper support is in place.

Suresh: A follow-up: I'll share early results in this thread by EOD. If we confirm numerical parity, we can ship canary to dedicated pools and monitor token-error rates.

Alex: Great. tagging incident label 'perf-regression' and creating the issue.
